reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in translating discrete game events into continuous fantasy point outcomes. The paper employs Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Neural Networks (NN) to map high-dimensional game statistics to scalar fantasy scores. SVR leverages kernel functions to capture non-linear patterns in player performance, while NNs adaptively learn complex feature interactions. Both methods operate under the assumption that past performance correlates with future outcomes within similar contexts. The feature selection process mitigates noise through Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross Validation (RFECV), enhancing generalization. However, the model's fidelity depends critically on data quality and representativeness—particularly given the limited dataset spanning only six seasons. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient data, misalignment between expert judgment and empirical signals, and exclusion of dynamic variables like injuries or strategic shifts. These limitations underscore the need for adaptive learning frameworks capable of incorporating real-time updates.
